On demand adds context when you open an article and request it. Automatic adds context to selected articles while creating the digest. The choice applies to the next run, including scheduled runs.
A profile sets the prompts and scoring rules. You can assign a profile to a source or let Horizon choose from the available profiles.
Enter a key or token under its variable name. Hovq saves the value on the VPS and shows only the names of saved secrets.
The protected backup contains configuration, profiles, secrets and the schedule. Keep its password for restoration. Digests and the journal are stored separately.
This order applies by default to the feed and archive. To sort the current view differently, use the filters at the top of the feed.
Downloaded digests and successfully saved covers are available offline. Covers that could not be retrieved are shown with a background.
Pick a source type to edit its list. Apply changes to save them on the VPS. A source test uses the last saved settings.
Horizon collects publications from this many hours before a run. The schedule controls when the run starts.
Limits how many materials can appear in one digest after filtering. Leaving this unset uses the group and profile rules alone.
Materials below this score do not pass this filter.
Limits the response length from the model. A very low limit can truncate summaries or structured responses.
Sets how many requests this stage can run at once. Lower it if your model provider often reports a rate limit.
Horizon can group materials about the same event and remove repeats from a digest.
Choose manual runs, a time on selected weekdays, or a repeating interval. The VPS follows the saved schedule independently of the phone.
The scheduled time follows the time zone you choose, even when the phone is in a different city.
